claims.text: Introducing elements with significantly different atomic radii will increase lattice distortion in a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
Increased lattice distortion produces a higher density of pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
A higher density of domain-wall pinning sites increases the coercive field.
The intervention will increase the coercive field by approximately 10–20% relative to a matched baseline with minimal lattice distortion.
The coercivity-increasing effect requires the alloy to remain a single-phase solid solution.
The coercivity-increasing effect requires the introduced elements to be randomly distributed.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on the identities and concentrations of the introduced elements.
A matched baseline and modified sample can be compared by measuring their coercive fields with a vibrating sample magnetometer.
Failure of the modified sample to have a significantly higher coercive field than the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
